messages:
Hannah Lowe: Quick announcement: Product is consolidating several small Jira projects into two canonical projects (ENG-CORE and ENG-PLAT) to reduce fragmentation and make cross-team reporting easier. Migration window: Sat Jul 10 03:00-07:00 UTC. Migration guide + mapping CSV: https://internal.redwood/migrations/jira-project-rekey-2026. Please review if you own issues or automation that reference project keys. @eng-platform @eng-sre

Priya Nair: Can you confirm whether issue keys will change? Our release notes link to ENGOPS-123 style keys in docs and it's painful to update them.

Hannah Lowe: Short answer: yes, many issue keys will be rekeyed to the new project prefix. We'll preserve a redirect map service that resolves old keys to new ones for 12 months (read-only redirects). However absolute links embedded in external docs won't automatically update. We'll publish a CSV and a small CLI to rewrite docs in bulk for owners.

Jira-bot: preflight checks: project-permissions -> PASS, webhook-subscriptions -> WARNING (11 webhooks reference legacy keys), issue-linking -> PASS. See /debug/jira-rekey-1829995555.

Marco Chen: CI/automation note: our release pipeline uses JIRA_PROJECT env to gate releases. If keys change, CI jobs will fail. We need a compatibility layer: env JIRA_PROJECT_LEGACY -> maps to new project. Also recommend teams add `jira validate` to preflight.

Lena Ortiz: DevEx: we'll add a migration helper script to rewrite references in markdown and release templates. Example usage:
```
# rewrite links in repo docs
./tools/jira-rewrite --map mapping.csv --dir docs/ --dry-run
```
We'll open PRs for the helper today.

Priya Nair: What about Jira automation rules and webhooks? We have automations that trigger when issue key matches ENG-OPS-.*

Hannah Lowe: We'll run a two-step migration for automations: 1) Duplicate rules with new project keys and run them in parallel (shadow mode) for 48h; 2) After validation, flip and delete legacy rules. Webhook consumers will get a 301-style redirect payload for old keys for 12 months. Owners should update listeners to accept the new key or follow redirect mapping.

Jira-bot: scheduled migration batch plan: batch1 internal repos (03:00-04:15), batch2 platform teams (04:30-05:45), batch3 GA (06:00-07:00). Post-checks: issue-link-resolve, webhook-delivery, automation-run-smoke.

Marco Chen: Artifacts & CI history: are we preserving attachments and comments? We must keep timestamps and authors intact for audits.

Hannah Lowe: Yes  attachments, comments, change history preserved. We will snapshot the projects pre-migration and keep an archival export. Audit trail will show the rekey operation and the actor. Retention: archived exports retained for 365 days.

Lena Ortiz: I've flagged migration-critical PRs: devex/jira-tools #51 (rewrite helper), infra/jira-sync #312 (redirect mapping service). Tagging owners for reviews.

support-bot: Support FYI: drafting canned responses and status page copy. Likely common questions: "Why is my issue key different?" and "How long will redirects last?" Will share draft by EOD Thu.

Priya Nair: Rollback plan?

Hannah Lowe: If we observe >2% link-resolution failures or >1% automation error rate sustained for 15m we will pause the cutover and revert automations to legacy rules and re-enable legacy project reads. Steps and steps to rehydrate previous state are in the runbook under "emergency-rollback".

Marco Chen: I'll add a CI smoke job that queries a sample of issues before and after and compares keys and statuses.

Hannah Lowe: Thanks all . Please add any owned project keys to the mapping CSV in the doc by EOD Fri. Office hours Fri 17:00 UTC. Ping @oncall-platform for preflight failures. :white_check_mark:"
